editorial:
Imagine waking up in a park and realizing you have no idea who you are, but you have a six-year-old son standing right there who needs you. That is the scary situation Saga finds herself in after a sudden seizure wipes her memory. You will feel her panic as she tries to fake it, pretending everything is normal so the government doesn't take her child away. It feels like a high-stakes puzzle where you are just as confused as she is, trying to piece together her life from old photos and strange clues left in her own home.

The acting is top-notch and really sells the confusion and fear of losing your identity. While the story moves a bit slow at first, the payoff is worth it because the twists actually make sense. If you enjoy mysteries that dig into family secrets, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: As Saga digs deeper, she remembers that her childhood was not what she thought. The twist is that she suffered a major trauma as a kid that she had blocked out to survive. The final scenes show her facing the truth about her parents and the abuse she endured. By accepting these painful memories, she finally stops hiding and finds a way to truly connect with her son and move forward with her life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological mysteries and emotional family stories.
